title: Tracing distinguishability through transformer processing with stochastic LayerNorm
abstract: arXiv:2608.30720v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Representational similarity is foundational to analyses of deep networks, yet distances between point-valued representations are not intrinsically tied to downstream function: nearby states may produce different behaviors, while distant states may behave similarly. We instead give representations volume, turning similarity into statistical distinguishability. Overlapping stochastic representations necessarily induce overlapping downstream distributions, grounding latent comparison in model function and bringing it under information-theoretic tools such as the data-processing inequality. We realize this idea in pretrained transformers through a light-touch modification to LayerNorm: at each residual-stream read, we normalize the state, add isotropic Gaussian noise, and renormalize. During distillation fine-tuning, one learned allocation parameter per residual-stream read distributes a fixed global rate budget across the processing stack.

translated_title: 通过随机LayerNorm追踪Transformer处理过程中的可区分性
translated_abstract: 表征相似性是深度网络分析的基础，然而点值表示之间的距离与下游功能并没有内在联系：相近的状态可能产生不同的行为，而相距较远的状态可能表现出相似的行为。我们转而赋予表示以“体积”，将相似性转化为统计可区分性。重叠的随机表示必然会导致重叠的下游分布，从而将潜在表征的比较建立在模型功能之上，并使其能够运用信息论工具（如数据处理不等式）进行分析。我们在预训练Transformer中通过对LayerNorm进行轻量级修改来实现这一想法：在每次读取残差流时，先对状态进行归一化，添加各向同性高斯噪声，然后重新归一化。在蒸馏微调过程中，每个残差流读取位置拥有一个可学习的分配参数，将固定的全局速率预算分配到整个处理堆栈中。
tldr: 该论文提出对LayerNorm进行随机化改造，为Transformer的表征赋予“体积”，将表征相似性转化为统计可区分性，使潜在表征比较与模型下游功能相联系，并可运用数据处理不等式等信息论工具进行分析。
